node22.scope: Current assertion differential, 25 lifecycle/protocol cases and 39 registry cases on macOS full Chromium with residency enabled.

newCoverage: Full visibility predicates observe CSS transform completion and a transient CSS visibility interval without DOM mutations.

An original zero-advance font served through a gated local HTTP response changes target geometry without DOM mutation; successful loads match and failed loads remain false. Separate isolated-registry fallback withholding proves loadingdone/loadingerror subscriptions run complete predicates.

Separate CDP targets outside the reference driver context map avoid its focus/visibility emulation. Freeze events, hidden visibility, and unchanged application/registry counters prove actual suspension; active recovery resumes property detection through the real timer fallback while animation frames remain stopped.
A finite renderer deadline that passes while frozen cannot become a late success after the app changes its input on resume. Explicit cancellation while frozen also cannot resurrect.
Public CSS animation and font-load assertions pass the shared Playwright/Flashwright differential with residency on/off in the core matrix.
Integrated cancellation checks now also require empty dirty queues, closed scheduling ports, and no queued flush callbacks.

fontFixture.purpose: An original minimal TrueType fixture with an empty, zero-advance A glyph. Loading it changes an inline-block target from the fallback glyph width to zero without modifying its text or DOM attributes.
fontFixture.runtimeDependency: None. Browser tests read the checked-in font bytes; fontTools is only needed to regenerate this fixture.

exploration.excludedClaim: An accepted freeze command against a visibility-emulated reference page did not actually suspend callbacks. That exploratory result is explicitly excluded from suspension coverage.

performanceCarryForward.scope: The production/runtime and benchmark sources and exact optimized macOS binary are unchanged. Prior paired snapshots retain their original source identities. No new speed claim or causal performance effect is attributed to these tests. The material complete-flow target remains open after the prior replication.
